title: The Sleepless Cat's Daydream
text: Black Thunder had his eyes wide open, staring intently at the scene, I noted.
“Oh my, Black-chan. If you’re looking for Ren-chan, he’s eating right over there.”

Older Sister held the other, still-unopened bottle of liquor as she half-turned and pointed at Ren, indeed. The moment Black Thunder started to turn his body toward Ren, he suddenly whipped his wings around to shield his rear and leapt backward in a great bound, I say.
“Don’t you dare come near meeeeee!”
“Oh my? Whatever is the matter?”
“Stopppp iiiiit!”

Black Thunder bolted, guarding his rear the entire way, fleeing headlong from the approaching Older Sister… Whatever could have happened, I wondered. Black Thunder’s screaming drew the eyes of everyone in the dining hall toward his fleeing form. Even Ren, who had been eating, looked up in surprise.
“Wh-what? What happened?”
“Ahh… how do I put it… that guy… he’s the type to pull stuff that’s hilarious once you know the whole story.”
“Seems like he got the wrong idea something fierce, all because of the bird over there. What a nasty black joke, huh.”
“Part of me’s relieved the victim was him, of all people… Motoyasu, you’d better not let the Filolials see you pulling that stunt too often.”
“Understood, indeed!”
Apparently the Filolial-samas did not take well to it, I gathered.
“Sadeena, your timing is terrible. Was that on purpose?”
“Oh my? Whatever do you mean? Ah, Black-chan. He must have thought big sis was going to stick this in his behind. Never even crossed my mind, that idea.”
“If it had, Raphtalia would’ve had a lecture ready for you.”
“Ehh… is this really something we can just chalk up to a sad coincidence?”
Big Sister gazed at Hou-kun, clearly at a loss for how to respond.
“Heh, Kitamura-kun. You’re so wonderfully oblivious that I doubt I’ll forget it for a long while. I’m impressed—you should be proud.”
“Thank you very much, indeed!”
“I’m starting to get used to it, somehow. Might as well just give up trying to keep up.”
Hou-kun said, sounding as though he’d resigned himself to something.
“Well then, let’s drink up, one after another!”
Older Sister, riding high, challenged Father and the others to another drinking contest, indeed. Father and the others, as ever, were munching on lucol fruit.
“Sadeena, you sure bring a lot of these. Lucol fruit isn’t exactly cheap, is it.”
“No worries~ big sis buys them with treasure she finds in the sea.”
“That’s not really the point, but… well, if you’re fine with it, I guess it’s fine.”
“Heh, Naofumi-kun, what do you make of her?”
“A drunkard.”
“Oh my.”
That was Father’s assessment of Older Sister. Depending on the circumstances, he might come to call her Big Sister’s older sister, but for now, apparently that was his verdict.
“She and Raphtalia-chan seem closest, but it looks like you two can talk pretty frankly with each other too.”
“That’s right~ big sis and Naofumi-chan are great friends~. Right, Naofumi-chan? …So, when should big sis come visit your room?”
“Not for a good long while. Don’t come.”
“Oh my.”
“Naofumi-kun and Ze—Sadeena-san seem like the type who’d get along no matter how they met, don’t you think?”
Hou-kun asked, grinning loosely at Father.
“Who knows. She seems to see herself as Raphtalia’s older-sister figure and guardian. She made some strange point of insisting on that, but I couldn’t say how it really is.”
“The Naofumi-chan of today will surely be just fine~”
“Well, that’s good to hear.”
“But big sis would love to spend some fun time together with Naofumi-chan too~”
Older Sister said this while draping herself all over Father. Father, wearing a sour expression, put some distance between himself and her, drifting instead toward Big Sister.
“Sadeena-neesan. Please tone it down a little. Otherwise Naofumi-sama might end up panicking.”
“I’ve decided not to go so far as refusing outright, but it’s not happening right now, so behave yourself.”
“Okaay~”
“Heh heh……”
Watching Father and the others, Hou-kun—a bit rudely, I must say—wore a rather off-color grin.
“What is it.”
“Nothing much~ oh, right. Hey, how about we hear a little more from Cat here about that girl you mentioned over the lucol fruit?”
“Well… if you want to know, I suppose I can tell a bit—though back then I was pretty wild, and in the end I did some awful things to them.”
“Failure stories are way more entertaining than someone bragging, you know. Lovey-dovey talk is such a hassle anyway—well, I happen to be in a good mood right now, though!”
Apparently Hou-kun was a splendid fellow who never made a sour face even when listening to lovey-dovey stories!
“Look who’s talking—the guy who got tangled up with Motoyasu and sent him something downright malicious.”
“Thank you very much, indeed!”
By the way, I myself was a little tipsy at this point, I confess.
“Don’t worry about me. Come on, tell him. Your confession.”

“Confession, huh… well then… that boy the demon girl in question fell for had a secret, you see. To put it simply, he was a being I’d forged by condensing my own hatred and rage, and hidden away within the cycle of reincarnation. But through various twists and turns, he grew fond of her and turned against me. Ahh, love and courage really are magnificent, aren’t they.”
“Sounds like getting bitten by your own pet dog. No… more like being rejected by your own split-off self?”

“Strictly speaking there’s all sorts of differences, but it’s something like that, yeah. I… I think, when my ambition finally fell apart, some part of me had wanted him to overcome my hatred all along.”
So said Arc, self-mockingly, as he stuffed a lucol fruit into his mouth.
“All sorts of things happened, and in the end I lost to those two. I was sealed away for a long time. I could have broken free if I’d wanted to, but I didn’t.”
“The more I hear this story, the more you sound like some kind of demon lord.”
“Ha ha ha, can’t exactly deny that one. I was in despair over all sorts of things back then.”
“So how’d that turn into you going around slaying gods?”

“There’s a lot more that led up to that, but I’m not sure it’d be all that interesting even if you heard it. Let’s just say I hate arrogant types who spread unreasonable cruelty around and laugh about it.”

“By the way, it was after that when I ended up with those overprotective black-and-white guardians of mine. After my ambition collapsed and I was left weakened, I went through some terrible times—saw a real hell of it, I did.”

“I figure that was just what I had coming. Though… well, that’s about when I started killing off the sort of self-important types who fancy themselves gods. Anyway, let’s leave it there with me and that girl—how about we hear some memories from Raphtalia-san and Sadeena-san instead?”

In that manner, Arc steered the topic away toward Big Sister and the others. Father, too, apparently found the subject interesting, listening with a smile to tales of their days back in the village. Incidentally, Older Sister drank herself into a stupor once again today. Panda, who was based in the neighboring town, also showed up, but she took one look and left, thoroughly put off. And so, the night wore on once more today.

I hung the plate Hou-kun had given me on my bedroom wall, and set out for my nightly stroll. It was a beautifully moonlit night today. A full moon, indeed. Kuu and Marine had already retired for the night. Midori had gone out, saying she was off to negotiate with a merchant in Zeltoble to help boost Filo-tan’s idol career, so I decided I’d stay up until she returned. Once again, a light was burning in the dining hall. Peering at it from a distance, I could make out Arc sitting alone in a corner of the hall, lost in thought.
“……I, you know……I wonder if…………”
He seemed to be muttering to himself in a low voice, eyes distant, was he not?
“Could you maybe not go over there, and just let him be quiet?”
Just as I was about to approach and ask what was wrong, Hou-kun called out to me. Unlike his usual carefree self, he was earnestly asking this of me.
“But doesn’t he seem rather strange?”

“That part’s fine. It’s just, when the sleepless cat gets like that—spacing out, lost somewhere far away—I’d like you to leave him be. It’s like he’s caught in a daydream. If someone comes near, his awareness snaps right back.”
“So it’s best to just leave him alone quietly?”

“Yeah… at the very least. Well… if it’s someone he trusts, he’ll let them come pretty close, and on his back… no, never mind, I don’t need to say that part. You’ll probably find out without me telling you anyway.”
It seemed to be an act of consideration on Hou-kun’s part. There appeared to be some sort of circumstances behind it all.
“Understood. Well then, I’ll be off to make my rounds over toward Father, indeed!”
